# The trust ledger

One file listing **everything outside our direct control that vbm-simd executes or depends on**: code we did not prove, code we did not write, and facilities we assume. It exists because
*verified by construction* is the first priority of the project: the size of the unverified base, and the care taken at its boundary, is the most important measure. A boundary with no entry here
does not land (`scripts/trust-ledger-check.sh`, Tier 1).

**Snapshot at the first landing:** no C and no `@[extern]`: the library was Lean only, and the kernels are proved against the machines of `docs/SPEC.md`. The ledger covered what the *build* depends on.

**Snapshot at the shims (T10):** the portable shim header `include/vbm_simd.h` (four `static inline` functions, about 60 lines of C with comments) is the first and only trusted C. The vector-instruction shims (AVX2, AVX-512, NEON, WebAssembly simd128) arrive in their own landings, **one entry each**, each with its Lean model and a differential test against the portable path.

## How the gate keeps this file true

The set of things that must appear here is **derived from the tree, not from this file**: every `@[extern]` symbol under `VbmSimd/`, every header under `include/`, the build
pins (`lean-toolchain`, `mise.toml`, `lakefile.lean`), the Lean pin's compiler, runtime and bundled clang/ld.lld (the keys `lean-compiler`,
`lean-runtime`, `clang-lld`), and a watch-list of tools the scripts run. Each is a key (`file:`, `extern:`, `tool:`, plus the three Lean keys) that an entry must name on its **Covers** line.
- A new boundary (extern, header, tool) with no entry **fails**. A `Covers` key that names nothing real fails, and **removing any entry fails** (the gate does this to itself on every run, one entry at a time: an entry that covers nothing required is padding).
  Dangling file references fail. An entry needs all seven fields, a **Plan** from `verify | replace | sandbox | accept` (`accept` needs `because ...`), **Assumes** that links a written contract or says `no written contract`
  (counted as a gap), and **Test** that names a test that can fail or says `none` (counted as a gap).
- Not covered by the gate (said here rather than pretended): a tool called from a script that is not on the watch-list in `scripts/trust-ledger-check.sh`, and the *quality* of an entry's prose.

Entry format: **What** it is; **Enters** where it enters; **Assumes** what we assume of it (the contract); **Test** the test that can fail; **Owner**; **Plan**; **Covers** the derived keys.

## The Lean toolchain (pinned: one Lean release for the whole tree)

### T01. The Lean compiler: frontend, kernel, C emitter
- **What:** the `lean` release pinned in `lean-toolchain` and `mise.toml`: the elaborator, the kernel that checks every proof, and `EmitC`, which turns the library's definitions into the C a consumer links. A kernel soundness bug would void the proofs; an emitter bug would give the C different semantics from the Lean. Nothing proves the emitter preserves semantics.
- **Enters:** `lean-toolchain`, `mise.toml`; every `.lean` file.
- **Assumes:** the kernel is sound and `EmitC` is faithful: no written contract beyond Lean's own documentation. The differential tests of the shims and the consumers' vectors are the check on the emitted code; nothing in this repository re-checks the kernel independently (nothing runs after the push).
- **Test:** none: the emitter is checked only by the consumers' tests; nothing runs after the push.
- **Owner:** upstream Lean (leanprover/lean4); the repository owner pins it (CODEOWNERS).
- **Plan:** accept, because there is no other mature route from Lean to C, WASM and the other targets and the kernel is small and nothing in this repository re-checks it independently any more, so the consumer's own build is the check; revisit when an extractor with a semantics-preservation proof exists.
- **Covers:** `lean-compiler` `file:lean-toolchain` `file:mise.toml`

### T03. The Lean runtime and its headers (lean.h, libleanrt)
- **What:** the C runtime every Lean-emitted C file links: reference counting, allocation, arrays and strings, big numbers. It is the lowest layer under the compiled kernels. This library's kernels are `UInt64` arithmetic (no allocation) so the part that runs is small; it is not checked by us.
- **Enters:** the Lean release pinned in `lean-toolchain`; the emitted C of `VbmSimd` includes `lean.h`.
- **Assumes:** the runtime implements Lean's object model correctly; no written contract.
- **Test:** none of ours: exercised through the consumers' tests.
- **Owner:** upstream Lean; the owner pins the version.
- **Plan:** accept, because the runtime is part of the one Lean release we pin and no verified replacement exists; the library imports `Init` only so the part that runs stays small.
- **Covers:** `lean-runtime`

### T04. clang and ld.lld (the compiler and linker the Lean release bundles)
- **What:** the C compiler and linker bundled in the Lean release, used by `lake`/`leanc` to compile Lean's emitted C. A miscompile changes the program the proofs were about.
- **Enters:** `lean-toolchain` (the bundle comes with the pin); `lakefile.lean` (every `lean_lib` build).
- **Assumes:** the compiler preserves C semantics for the emitted code; no written contract.
- **Test:** none of ours today; the check is the consumers' vectors run against the compiled artifact, and the differential tests the shims will carry.
- **Owner:** upstream LLVM via the Lean release; the owner pins it.
- **Plan:** sandbox. Check compiled artifacts against the Lean models with a differential test run before the push, never trust the compile.
- **Covers:** `clang-lld`

## The build and process tools

### T05. Lake and the build file
- **What:** `lake` (shipped in the Lean release) reads `lakefile.lean` and builds both libraries; the file sets `warningAsError` and `autoImplicit false` and declares the two module roots (`VbmSimd`, `VbmSimdProofs`), the first Init-only.
- **Enters:** `lakefile.lean`; every `lake build` and `lake env lean --run` in `scripts/`.
- **Assumes:** the build builds the files that are in the tree and nothing else; the root split and the Init-only rule are enforced by Tier 1, not by Lake (scripts/tier1.sh: the import scan).
- **Test:** scripts/tier1.sh (zero-warning check with its negative case; the import scan with its negative cases).
- **Owner:** the repository owner (CODEOWNERS: `lakefile.lean`).
- **Plan:** accept, because Lake is the Lean toolchain's own build tool and a change to it is a toolchain change (T01).
- **Covers:** `file:lakefile.lean` `tool:lake`

### T06. mise: installs the pinned Lean release
- **What:** `mise` downloads and installs the Lean release tarball named in `mise.toml` from GitHub releases and puts it on `PATH` for `mise exec -- ...`.
- **Enters:** `mise.toml`; every script is run as `mise exec -- scripts/...`.
- **Assumes:** the tarball is the one released for that tag; no checksum is verified by us today (no written contract): a supply-chain gap.
- **Test:** none: nothing here can fail if the tarball were swapped (a gap, counted).
- **Owner:** the repository owner (`mise.toml`); mise is upstream.
- **Plan:** sandbox. Pin the release checksum in a lockfile once there is a place to keep it; until then the tarball's integrity is GitHub's.
- **Covers:** `tool:mise`

### T07. python3: the process tooling
- **What:** `python3`, the trust-ledger checker. It runs on the developer's machine before the push; it is not part of any artifact.
- **Enters:** `scripts/trust_ledger.py`, run by `scripts/trust-ledger-check.sh` (Tier 1).
- **Assumes:** it does what its manual says; the self-tests of the checker are the check that our use is right; no written contract.
- **Test:** scripts/spec-check.sh, and the checker's own self-tests (it removes each entry in turn and requires a failure).
- **Owner:** upstream tools; the repository owner approves the scripts (CODEOWNERS).
- **Plan:** accept, because it touches the process and not the artifact: a compromised interpreter could pass a ledger that the tree does not support, which the gate's own self-tests and the owner's review are there to catch.
- **Covers:** `tool:python3`

## The trusted C

### T10. The portable shim header: include/vbm_simd.h (`ld64`, `st64`, `st32`, `ctz`)
- **What:** the first 60 lines of `include/vbm_simd.h` (the byte search below is T11): four `static inline` functions, each the body of an `@[extern]` function of `VbmSimd/Shims.lean` whose Lean body is its specification (the model): `vbm_simd_ld64` (an 8-byte little-endian load from a Lean `ByteArray`, zero past the end), `vbm_simd_st64` and `vbm_simd_st32` (8- and 4-byte little-endian stores, in place when the array is unshared, copied first when shared, nothing written past the end), `vbm_simd_ctz` (count of trailing zero bits, 64 for zero; `__builtin_ctzll`). They exist because Lean's emitted C for byte-at-a-time assembly is 2.4 times slower than one load or store. Each is total (no out-of-range access, no precondition), moves or counts bits and decides nothing. A wrong load, a store through a shared array, or a miscount would be a bug no Lean proof sees: they are the unverified base of every kernel built on them.
- **Enters:** `include/vbm_simd.h`; every consumer compiles its generated C with `-include include/vbm_simd.h` (the repository's own `shim-test` and the `lean_lib` do, `lakefile.lean`); the four `@[extern]` symbols `vbm_simd_ld64`, `vbm_simd_st64`, `vbm_simd_st32`, `vbm_simd_ctz`.
- **Assumes:** the Lean models of `VbmSimd/Shims.lean` (the specification, in `docs/SPEC.md` clauses VS-5 and VS-6); a little-endian host with GCC or clang builtins (the header refuses others at compile time); the Lean runtime's `lean_sarray_*` functions behave as `lean.h` documents (T03); a Lean `ByteArray` is a scalar array of bytes.
- **Test:** `scripts/test-shims.sh` runs `tests/ShimTest.lean` (about 32000 comparisons of each C function against its model: every array size 0 to 41 with every index through, at and past the end including the largest `USize`; every single-bit and bit-pair word for `ctz`, 20000 random; a shared array must be copied) and then builds six deliberate mutants of the header (a wrong offset, a skipped copy-on-share, a wrong zero case, two skipped partial stores) in scratch copies, each of which the same test must catch (T11 and T12 add their own mutants to the same list).
- **Owner:** the repository owner (CODEOWNERS: `include/`).
- **Plan:** verify, in part: exhaustive testing is impossible for 64-bit inputs, so the argument is the boundary and random cases plus mutants; a formal model of the C (a verified C compiler's semantics) would replace the argument and is out of scope. The header stays small on purpose.
- **Covers:** `file:include/vbm_simd.h` `extern:vbm_simd_ld64` `extern:vbm_simd_st64` `extern:vbm_simd_st32` `extern:vbm_simd_ctz`

### T11. The AVX2 byte search and the CPU test: include/vbm_simd.h (`vbm_simd_find_avx2`, `vbm_simd_has_avx2`)
- **What:** about 55 more lines of the same header: `vbm_simd_find_avx2`, the C body of `findAvx2` (`VbmSimd/Find.lean`), the first index at or after `i` of a byte in a set of at most four bytes, `n` (the size) when there is none or `i >= n`; 32 bytes per step with one 256-bit compare per member (clang vector extensions and `__builtin_ia32_pmovmskb256`: the Lean toolchain ships no intrinsics header), the last partial step done by one load of the last 32 bytes of the array with the bits of the bytes before `i` shifted out, arrays under 32 bytes by the scalar loop `vbm_simd_find_scalar` (which is also the whole function on a CPU or compiler without the AVX2 body). `vbm_simd_has_avx2` (CPUID leaf 7 AVX2 bit, leaf 1 OSXSAVE and AVX bits, XCR0 bits 1 and 2) is the C body of `hasAvx2`; `findFirstOf` takes the shim only when it says yes and otherwise runs `findSwar`, which is Lean, proved, and not trusted. The shim decides nothing the model does not: its Lean body is `findSpec` (`[VS-11]`), and `findFirstOf_spec` is proved for either answer of the CPU test. A wrong index, a read past the end (a fault, or a silent wrong answer from bytes that are not the array's), a dropped member or a wrong CPU answer (AVX2 instructions on a CPU without them: SIGILL) would be bugs no Lean proof sees.
- **Enters:** `include/vbm_simd.h`; the two `@[extern]` symbols `vbm_simd_find_avx2` and `vbm_simd_has_avx2` (`VbmSimd/Find.lean`); every consumer that calls `findFirstOf`, compiled with `-include include/vbm_simd.h` as for T10.
- **Assumes:** the model `findSpec` (`docs/SPEC.md` clause VS-11); an x86-64 CPU's `cpuid` and `xgetbv` report truthfully, and an AVX2 CPU with the OS saving the vector state runs the instructions the compiler emits for `target("avx2")`; clang's vector extensions compile `==`, `|` on 32-byte vectors to compare and or (the compiler is T04); `lean_sarray_cptr` and `lean_sarray_size` describe the array (T03). On aarch64 with clang `has_avx2` is 0, `vbm_simd_find_avx2` is the scalar loop and the search a consumer reaches is the NEON one (T15); any other build is the scalar loop, which the tests (and the guard test) exercise on every size.
- **Test:** `scripts/test-shims.sh` runs `tests/ShimTest.lean` (about 17 million comparisons: the AVX2 shim, the proved portable search and the dispatch against `findSpec` for four sets, every size 0 to 70 and the boundaries 95 to 97, 127 to 129, 255 to 257 and 1000, a member planted at every position or none, every byte a member, random dense arrays, every start through past the end and the largest `USize`; `hasAvx2` against the `avx2` flag of `/proc/cpuinfo`) and `tests/find_guard.c` (about 11 million cases of the C functions against a naive loop on buffers flush against an unmapped page at the end and at the start, so any read outside the buffer is a SIGSEGV), then ten deliberate mutants of the header (an over-read, bits kept from before the start, a shift off by one, a dropped member, no bounds guard, a wrong tail load, a wrong index, a dropped scalar member, a scalar loop that restarts, a wrong CPUID bit), each of which one of the two must catch.
- **Owner:** the repository owner (CODEOWNERS: `include/`).
- **Plan:** verify, in part: the test is the boundary, planted and random cases plus guard pages and mutants, not a proof of the C; the portable path is proved in Lean, so a doubt about the shim is settled by taking it out (the dispatch falls back to `findSwar`). The other vector sets each get their own entry (NEON: T15; AVX-512 and simd128: not yet).
- **Covers:** `extern:vbm_simd_find_avx2` `extern:vbm_simd_has_avx2`

### T12. The AVX2 membership masks: include/vbm_simd.h (`vbm_simd_inset64`)
- **What:** about 45 more lines of the same header: `vbm_simd_inset64`, the C body of `inset64` (`VbmSimd/Inset.lean`), the 64-bit mask of the block of 64 bytes at `i` whose bit `p` says that byte `i + p` is a member of a set of at most four bytes (as in T11), 0 for a byte at or past the end and for an `i` at or past the end. It is the classifier of a structural scanner (quote, backslash, operator, white space masks of every block): two 256-bit loads, one compare per member (clang vector extensions and `__builtin_ia32_pmovmskb256`), one movemask each; a block that crosses the end is the last 64 bytes of the array (all inside it) with the bits of the bytes before `i` shifted out, an array under 64 bytes the scalar loop `vbm_simd_inset64_scalar` (which is also the whole function on a CPU or compiler without the AVX2 body). It uses T11's CPU test: a consumer calls it only where `hasAvx2 ()` is true and runs its own proved portable kernel otherwise, so the shim decides nothing the model does not: its Lean body is `insetSpec` (`[VS-12]`). A wrong mask bit, a read past the end or a dropped member would be bugs no Lean proof sees (a consumer's proof takes the model for the C).
- **Enters:** `include/vbm_simd.h`; the `@[extern]` symbol `vbm_simd_inset64` (`VbmSimd/Inset.lean`); every consumer that calls `inset64`, compiled with `-include include/vbm_simd.h` as for T10.
- **Assumes:** the model `insetSpec` (`docs/SPEC.md` clause VS-12); the CPU-test assumptions of T11 (the AVX2 instructions run where `hasAvx2 ()` says so); clang's vector extensions compile `==` and `|` on 32-byte vectors to compare and or (T04); `lean_sarray_cptr` and `lean_sarray_size` describe the array (T03). On aarch64 with clang the same symbol `vbm_simd_inset64` has the NEON body of T15; any other build is the scalar loop, exercised by Tier 1 only through the guard test, which runs it on every size.
- **Test:** `scripts/test-shims.sh` runs `tests/ShimTest.lean` (the AVX2 masks against `insetSpec` for nine sets, among them the set that contains the byte 0 and the JSON classes, every size 0 to 140 and the boundaries 191 to 193, 255 to 257 and 1000, a member planted at every position or at the lane and block boundaries, every byte a member, all zero, random dense arrays, every start through past the end and the largest `USize`; every byte value at the lane boundaries 0, 1, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 62 to 65 for every set) and `tests/find_guard.c` (the C functions against a naive loop on buffers flush against an unmapped page at the end and at the start, so any read outside the buffer is a SIGSEGV), then seven deliberate mutants of the header (an over-read, bits kept from before the start, a dropped member, no bounds guard, a wrong tail load, a wrong short-array case, a scalar loop that ignores the start), each of which one of the two must catch.
- **Owner:** the repository owner (CODEOWNERS: `include/`).
- **Plan:** verify, in part, as T11: the test is the boundary, planted, per-byte and random cases plus guard pages and mutants, not a proof of the C; the consumer's portable path is proved in Lean, so a doubt about the shim is settled by taking it out (the dispatch falls back to the portable kernel).
- **Covers:** `extern:vbm_simd_inset64`

### T13. The short append: include/vbm_simd.h (`vbm_simd_append`)
- **What:** about 35 more lines of the same header: `vbm_simd_append`, the C body of `appendBytes` (`VbmSimd/Append.lean`): the bytes `a[i, i + n)` appended to a Lean `ByteArray` `t`, the value of the runtime's `copySlice` at the end of `t`. For at most 32 bytes, an unshared `t` with room in its capacity and a run inside `a` (`vbm_simd_append_fits`, a predicate on five integers) it moves the run with two loads and two stores that overlap (`vbm_simd_move_short`: 16 (two words), 8, 4, 2 or 1 bytes at each end of the run, reading only `a[i, i + n)` and writing only `t[size, size + n)`) and sets the new size (`lean_sarray_set_size`; the function is `noinline`: in a consumer's parse loop the call measured faster than the inlined body; the general case is a function of its own, `vbm_simd_append_slow`, so that the fast path needs no prologue: about 28 instructions instead of 40); in every other case (a longer run, a shared `t`, no room, a run that ends past the end of `a`) it is the runtime's `lean_byte_array_copy_slice`, so the shim decides nothing the model does not: its Lean body is `copySlice` (`[VS-13]`, `appendBytes_spec`). It exists because the runtime call (an exclusiveness and capacity check, then `memcpy`) costs about 40 cycles for the few bytes of a number or a short string, a measurable share of a parse. A move outside the run, a write into a shared array or a wrong size would be bugs no Lean proof sees (a consumer's proof takes the model for the C).
- **Enters:** `include/vbm_simd.h`; the `@[extern]` symbol `vbm_simd_append` (`VbmSimd/Append.lean`); every consumer that calls `appendBytes`, compiled with `-include include/vbm_simd.h` as for T10.
- **Assumes:** the model (`docs/SPEC.md` clause VS-13); `lean_sarray_size`, `lean_sarray_capacity`, `lean_sarray_cptr`, `lean_sarray_set_size` and `lean_is_exclusive` describe the array as `lean.h` documents (T03); the declaration of `lean_byte_array_copy_slice` in the header is the runtime's (the generated C declares it with the same type).
- **Test:** `scripts/test-shims.sh` runs `tests/ShimTest.lean` (the compiled `appendBytes` against the model on an unshared and on a shared destination, for every combination of 6 prefixes, 6 spare capacities, 12 source sizes, every start through the end and far past it, and lengths 0 to 35, 40, 100 and the largest `USize`: the original of a shared array must be untouched) and `tests/find_guard.c` (`vbm_simd_append_fits` against its plain statement in 128-bit arithmetic on 17 edge values of each of its five arguments; `vbm_simd_move_short` for 0 to 32 bytes with the source and the destination each flush against an unmapped page, so that any read or write outside the run is a SIGSEGV, and between sentinels), then eleven deliberate mutants of the header (no room check, no source check, a limit of 33, a wrong offset of the second store and of the second load, seven bytes moved as eight, an append into a shared array, a size one too large, no size update), each of which one of the two must catch.
- **Owner:** the repository owner (CODEOWNERS: `include/`).
- **Plan:** verify, in part, as T10: the test is the boundary, planted and exhaustive-over-edges cases plus guard pages and mutants, not a proof of the C; a doubt about the shim is settled by making `appendBytes` call `copySlice` (the model) in the consumer. The header stays small on purpose.
- **Covers:** `extern:vbm_simd_append`

### T14. The AVX2 class masks: include/vbm_simd.h (`vbm_simd_classify64`)
- **What:** about 70 more lines of the same header: `vbm_simd_classify64`, the C body of `classify64` (`VbmSimd/Classify.lean`): for the block of 64 bytes at `i` of a Lean `ByteArray`, four 64-bit masks at once, stored as the words 0 to 3 of a fourth array `out` (in place when unshared, copied first when shared, a word only where its eight bytes lie inside `out`). A byte `v` has the class bits `t[v & 15] & t[16 + (v >> 4)]` (the 32 bytes of nibble tables `t` and the four mask bytes in `ms` are the caller's: what a class is stays in the consumer's Lean), and mask `r` has bit `j` set iff byte `i + j` exists and its class bits meet mask byte `r`. It is the classifier of a structural scanner (T12 asks one question per call and re-reads the block each time; here one call answers four): two 256-bit loads, two byte shuffles per half (`__builtin_ia32_pshufb256`, the tables broadcast to both lanes, the high nibble by a 16-bit shift and a mask), a compare with zero and a movemask per mask (clang vector extensions and builtins), the zero-padded copy of a table shorter than 32 bytes (the model reads zero past the end), and the scalar loop `vbm_simd_class_scalar` for a block that does not lie wholly inside the array and for every build without the AVX2 body. It uses T11's CPU test: a consumer calls it only where `hasAvx2 ()` is true on x86-64 and runs its own proved portable kernel otherwise. The shim decides nothing the model does not: its Lean body is `classifyModel` (`[VS-14]`). A wrong mask bit, a read outside the array or the table, a write outside `out` or into a shared array would be bugs no Lean proof sees (a consumer's proof takes the model for the C).
- **Enters:** `include/vbm_simd.h`; the `@[extern]` symbol `vbm_simd_classify64` (`VbmSimd/Classify.lean`); every consumer that calls `classify64`, compiled with `-include include/vbm_simd.h` as for T10.
- **Assumes:** the model `classifyModel` (`docs/SPEC.md` clause VS-14); the CPU-test assumptions of T11; clang's vector extensions and the `pshufb`/`pmovmskb` builtins compile as documented (T04); `lean_sarray_cptr`, `lean_sarray_size` and `lean_sarray_ensure_exclusive` describe the arrays as `lean.h` documents (T03). On aarch64 with clang the same symbol `vbm_simd_classify64` has the NEON body of T15; any other build is the scalar loop, which `tests/ShimTest.lean` runs there (neither vector body is compiled).
- **Test:** `scripts/test-shims.sh` runs `tests/ShimTest.lean` (the compiled `classify64` against the model: the JSON tables, the zero table, the all-ones table, random tables, a table of 20, of 3 and of 0 bytes, six mask words, every array size 0 to 140 and the boundaries 191 to 193, 255 to 257 and 1000 with random contents, every start through past the end and the largest `USize`; every byte value at the lane boundaries for the JSON table; `out` of every size 0 to 40, unshared and shared: the original of a shared array must be untouched) and `tests/find_guard.c` (the scalar words, and the AVX2 words for a block wholly inside the array, against a naive loop on an array and a 32-byte table each flush against an unmapped page at the end and at the start, so any read outside either is a SIGSEGV), then eleven deliberate mutants of the header (an over-read, the low-nibble lookup indexed by the high nibble, a wrong shift, a dropped mask, a missing inversion, the second half not shifted into place, a wrong scalar table lookup, a store into a shared destination on the fast path and on the slow one, a store of a word that does not wholly fit, a fast path taken for an `out` of 24 bytes), each of which one of the two must catch.
- **Owner:** the repository owner (CODEOWNERS: `include/`).
- **Plan:** verify, in part, as T12: the test is the boundary, planted, per-byte and random cases plus guard pages and mutants, not a proof of the C; the consumer's portable path is proved in Lean, so a doubt about the shim is settled by taking it out (the dispatch falls back to the portable kernel).
- **Covers:** `extern:vbm_simd_classify64`

### T15. The NEON bodies: include/vbm_simd.h (`vbm_simd_find_neon`, `vbm_simd_has_neon`, and the NEON bodies of `vbm_simd_inset64` and `vbm_simd_classify64`)
- **What:** about 90 more lines of the same header, compiled only for aarch64 with clang (`#elif defined(__aarch64__) && defined(__clang__)`): the NEON counterparts of T11, T12 and T14, with the same Lean models and the same contracts (total, never a read outside the array, the first-index and mask semantics of `findSpec`, `insetSpec`, `classifyModel`). `vbm_simd_find_neon` is the C body of `findNeon` (`VbmSimd/Find.lean`; the first index at or after `i` of a byte of a set of at most four bytes, `n` when none): 32 bytes per step as two 16-byte vectors, one compare per member, a horizontal maximum to test for a hit, the first flagged byte from the compare result narrowed to four bits per byte (`shrn`) and a `ctz`; the last partial step is one load of the last 16 bytes of the array with the nibbles of the bytes before `i` shifted out; arrays under 16 bytes the scalar loop. The same symbols `vbm_simd_inset64` and `vbm_simd_classify64` have, on aarch64, bodies of 16-byte vectors: four loads, compares per member (T12), or two table lookups per 16 bytes (`tbl`; the tables are one register each, the low nibble `x & 15`, the high nibble `x >> 4`), a `cmtst` per mask (T14); a block of 64 bytes is packed to one bit per byte by `vbm_neon_mask64` (each compare result and-ed with its bit weight, then pairwise adds of adjacent bytes: no movemask exists); a block that crosses the end is read as the last 64 bytes of the array with the bits before `i` shifted out (T12) or is the scalar loop (T14). `vbm_simd_has_neon` is the C body of `hasNeon`: a compile-time fact (1 on aarch64 with clang: NEON is part of the aarch64 base architecture, so there is no CPU test; 0 everywhere else). `findFirstOf` takes the NEON search when `hasNeon ()`, and `findFirstOf_spec` is proved for every answer of the two CPU facts; a consumer of `inset64` and `classify64` calls them where `hasAvx2 () || hasNeon ()` and runs its own proved portable kernel otherwise. The toolchain ships no `arm_neon.h`: the code uses clang's vector extensions and `__builtin_neon_vqtbl1q_v`, `__builtin_neon_vpaddq_v`, `__builtin_neon_vmaxvq_u8`, `__builtin_neon_vshrn_n_v`, the builtins `arm_neon.h` itself expands to. A wrong index, a read past the end, a dropped member, a wrong bit weight or a wrong table lookup would be bugs no Lean proof sees.
- **Enters:** `include/vbm_simd.h`; the `@[extern]` symbols `vbm_simd_find_neon` and `vbm_simd_has_neon` (`VbmSimd/Find.lean`) and, on aarch64, `vbm_simd_inset64` (T12) and `vbm_simd_classify64` (T14); every consumer compiled with `-include include/vbm_simd.h` as for T10.
- **Assumes:** the models `findSpec`, `insetSpec` and `classifyModel` (`docs/SPEC.md` clauses VS-11, VS-12, VS-14); an aarch64 CPU runs the Advanced SIMD instructions clang emits (they are baseline, ARMv8-A); clang's vector extensions compile `==`, `|`, `&`, `>>` on 16-byte vectors to compare, or, and, shift, and the four builtins above to `tbl`, `addp`, `umaxv`, `shrn` (T04); `lean_sarray_cptr` and `lean_sarray_size` describe the arrays (T03).
- **Test:** `scripts/test-shims.sh` on an aarch64 machine (the only machine that runs the NEON bodies) runs `tests/ShimTest.lean` with the same cases as T11, T12 and T14 (the search, the dispatch, the membership masks and the class masks against their models; `hasNeon` against the target) and refuses a run in which the NEON comparisons were not executed and counted, per kernel (`vec_ran`, with its own self-test); `tests/find_guard.c` runs the NEON search, membership masks and class words against a naive loop on buffers flush against an unmapped page at the end and at the start (it must report `neon checked`); then 26 deliberate mutants of the header (an over-read, bits kept from before the start, a shift off by one, a dropped member, no bounds guard, a wrong tail load, a wrong index, the second vector reported as the first, a wrong nibble width and narrowing shift, a wrong CPU fact, a wrong bit weight and pairing order, a wrong table lookup, shift, half or mask), each of which one of the two must catch. The shim test also prints a bench of the NEON bodies against the portable code in the same process; it is informational. On x86-64 the NEON bodies are not compiled and their mutants are not run.
- **Owner:** the repository owner (CODEOWNERS: `include/`).
- **Plan:** verify, in part, as T11, T12 and T14: the test is the boundary, planted, per-byte and random cases plus guard pages and mutants, not a proof of the C; the portable path is proved in Lean, so a doubt about a NEON body is settled by taking it out (`findFirstOf` falls back to `findSwar`, a consumer to its portable kernel).
- **Covers:** `extern:vbm_simd_find_neon` `extern:vbm_simd_has_neon`
